topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic and sets expectations regarding complement's complexity and nomenclature.

topics.label: Fundamentals, nomenclature, and central mechanism of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the overall purpose, naming rules, and the central role of C3 cleavage that underpin the complement system.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the three upstream recognition pathways and how they deposit convertases to reach the complement activation threshold.

topics.label: Downstream effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three primary effector outcomes driven by activated complement: opsonization, inflammation, and membrane attack complex lysis.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that prevent complement from damaging host cells.

topics.label: Clinical manifestations of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the distinct clinical phenotypes and diseases that result from deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how pathogens evade complement attack, using Staphylococcus aureus as a primary model.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the next topic in the course series.
